subject: Request to Recalculate Uptime After Edge Maintenance Overlap (NexusEdge)
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@nexusedge.io
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Hi Sofia,

We observed partial degradations across our read/write paths on 2027-05-03 between ~02:10 and 03:27 UTC and believe a CDN partner maintenance that ran during that window was the root cause. Our monitoring shows 4.8% availability loss for our API traffic routed through your eu-central region during that time, which exceeds our expected SLO.

Attached is our incident timeline and the probe dump from our synthetic checks. Can Redwood recalculate the uptime tally and tell us how maintenance attribution was applied? We want the formal uptime calculation and any credit recommendation.

Attachments: nexusedge_incident_timeline.pdf, nexusedge_probe_dump.csv

Thanks,
Alex Taylor
Head of Platform Ops
NexusEdge
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Alex — thanks for the timeline and probe data. I’m pulling the Redwood side metrics and will cross-check probe coverage (our probe fanout, ingress logs, and KV cache hit rates) across the interval.

A few quick asks to help speed this up:
- Can you confirm the exact public prefixes/ingress points affected (we need IP prefixes or POP IDs).
- Do the NexusEdge probes show 100% request failure or partial degraded latency for different endpoints?
- Any contract language / SLO text you want us to use in the calculation? We’ll default to the standard Hosted API SLA unless you point us to another commitment.

I’ve looped in Marissa (account lead) for commercial coordination and Vivek (infra) for the technical reconciliation. Expect an initial reconciliation by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Director — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@nexusedge.io
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Sofia — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and attached extra logs:
- Affected prefixes: 185.62.48.0/22 (POP-eu-central-3) and 185.62.52.0/22 (POP-eu-central-4).
- Impact profile: our synthetic checks show ~40% increased latency on write endpoints and ~18% 5xx error rate on read endpoints — not total outage. Some paths were fully unaffected.
- Contract: we reference the Hosted API SLA (v1.2) that we each signed in Jan 2026 — I’ve attached the excerpt in the probe dump file.

We believe that because only a subset of traffic was affected, the uptime tally should apportion the maintenance window proportionally to impacted prefixes/paths rather than full-window exclusion. Based on our probe coverage, we are estimating a 0.9% uptime hit attributable to Redwood and asking for a commensurate credit.

I can join a call if that helps; our SREs are available at 14:00 CEST today.

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Alex — appreciate the data. I reviewed NexusEdge’s probe dump alongside our ingress and path metrics. Preliminary findings:
- Redwood’s eu-central frontends did see increased latency coincident with the CDN maintenance window, but several of the affected prefixes are announced by the CDN partner, not Redwood’s network.
- Our probe fanout shows only ~57% overlap between NexusEdge’s failing checks and Redwood’s failing traces — i.e., not all customer-observed errors show up in our telemetry.

Proposed approach:
1) Reconcile probe coverage and determine overlap percentage (we have colleagues running a side-by-side trace comparison).
2) Attribute any time when only third-party prefixes were degraded to the CDN partner (full exclusion).
3) Where degradation is seen in both NexusEdge and Redwood traces, apply proportional apportionment using the overlap metric.

Commercially, we can offer a one-time credit while we complete the detailed reconciliation. I’d like to avoid overcommitting until Vivek confirms whether any Redwood path-level issue contributed more than transitive latency. Suggested temporary goodwill: 25% of the requested credit pending final apportionment. If the reconciliation favors you more, we’ll adjust upward.

Proposed next steps: 1) Technical sync at 14:00 CEST; 2) Redwood to deliver reconciliation report within 48 hours after the sync.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:35:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Looping in some technical detail after reviewing packet captures and egress BGP traces. Key points:
- During 02:10–03:27 UTC we see the CDN partner withdraw and reannounce a handful of prefixes; outbound routing changes caused transient RTT increases. Redwood’s frontends remained healthy (no JVM OOMs, no service restarts) and autoscaling kept request success rate above 93% for the majority of POPs.
- Where NexusEdge saw higher 5xx rates, our edge logs show either: (a) downstream 502/504 from the CDN cache tier, or (b) long tail latency into specific origin clusters where the CDN forwarded requests. That indicates the main failure mode is third-party cache/origin behavior, not a Redwood runtime bug.

Attached: edge-trace-logs.csv (sampled request traces), and a short reconciliation matrix I ran locally.

Given the asymmetric coverage and the evidence that the CDN partner caused the majority of the disruption, my recommendation is:
- Exclude pure third-party prefix withdrawals from Redwood uptime calculations;
- For overlapping failures where both sides show errors, apportion credit using the overlap ratio (we measured ~43% overlap for the sample window).

Operationally, if we apply Marissa’s goodwill offer (25%) and then finalize reconciliation to confirm overlap, we can settle quickly. I’ll prepare the formal reconciliation docs by EOD and hand to Legal/Commercial for sign-off.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE — Inference Runtime
Attachments: edge-trace-logs.csv
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@nexusedge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 15:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: uptime recalc after CDN maintenance overlap

Thanks all — the analysis and transparency are appreciated. NexusEdge will accept the 25% goodwill credit now and await the final reconciliation. Please send the formal credit memo and a DocuSign for the adjustment. Once we sign we’ll close the incident on our side.

Action items I see:
- Redwood to provide credit memo + DocuSign (Marissa will own).
- Final reconciliation report (Vivek) attached to the credit memo within 48 hours.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
